1. Scientific Analysis

In-situ VT powder XRD of sodium ibuprofen dihydrate heated under N2 (5-45 deg 2theta, Cu Kalpha) was fit at six temperatures (28.7-65.7C) with a uniform split pseudo-Voigt + SNIP model, all achieving global R2~0.9994-0.9995. The dominant, well-constrained finding is a discontinuous dehydration phase transition centered near 44.6C. Below the transition (28.7-40.9C) the pattern is dominated by hydrate reflections (strong ~11.0 and ~22.2 deg); above it (55.8-65.7C) these vanish entirely and a distinct product reflection set (~11.9, ~15.95, ~19.99 deg) dominates. Index 3 (48.3C) is a genuine coexistence frame (product fraction 0.735) showing both phases. The order parameter built from integrated areas is monotonic and model-robust (product fraction 0.067->0.067->0.097->0.735->1.0->1.0), providing the clearest transition signature. Peak positions are essentially static within each phase, ruling out continuous lattice expansion as the dominant effect; the reflection-count drop (27-28 to 17-22) reflects the product having a different, fewer-reflection cell rather than detection noise, because the count change coincides exactly with the area crossover. Crystallite-size reporting is not interpretable here: instrumental FWHM was set to 0 so all Scherrer sizes are lower bounds, the mean-size-vs-T trend is essentially flat/noisy (R2=0.08), no Williamson-Hall analysis was run, and per-peak sizes span >3x in the transition frames, consistent with mixed-phase broadening where an isotropic mean is an oversimplification. A few fitted components in indices 3-5 are physically dubious (FWHM 0.066 deg -> Scherrer 123 nm; a peak with amplitude ~1e-7 and FWHM 0.12 deg; several eta pinned at 0 or 1), and should be disregarded as unconstrained/cosmetic rather than treated as physical. The next logical step is phase identification (structure_matching/xrd) on the low-T and high-T end members to assign the hydrate and anhydrous/product structures, passing in the refined FWHMs.

Positions are static within each phase (hydrate ~22.2 deg, product ~20 deg), indicating whole-phase replacement rather than continuous lattice thermal expansion.

Trend: stable
Scattered 26-31.6 nm with negligible slope (R2=0.08); not interpretable because instrumental FWHM=0 (sizes are lower bounds) and transition frames mix two phases.

5. Scientific Claims

Claim 1: Sodium ibuprofen dihydrate undergoes a discontinuous dehydration phase transition centered near 44.6C under N2, evidenced by disappearance of hydrate reflections (~11.0, ~22.2 deg) and growth of a distinct product reflection set (~11.9, ~15.95, ~19.99 deg), with two-phase coexistence at 48.3C and a sigmoidal area-based product fraction (0.07->0.10->0.74->1.0).

Scientific Impact: Locates the dehydration temperature and demonstrates a first-order (coexistence) rather than continuous transformation, which is directly relevant to processing, storage stability, and solid-form control of a pharmaceutical salt.

Literature Search Query: Has anyone determined the dehydration transition temperature and mechanism (coexistence vs continuous) of sodium ibuprofen dihydrate under inert atmosphere by in-situ powder XRD?

Keywords: sodium ibuprofen dihydrate, dehydration, phase transition, in-situ XRD, pharmaceutical solid form, coexistence

6. Caveats & Limitations

Instrumental FWHM was set to 0, so all Scherrer sizes are lower bounds and the mean-size-vs-T trend (R2=0.08) is not interpretable; no Williamson-Hall analysis was performed. Per-peak sizes span >3x in the transition frames, consistent with mixed-phase broadening, so an isotropic Scherrer mean is an oversimplification. Several fitted components in indices 3-5 are unconstrained/cosmetic (e.g. FWHM 0.066 deg -> 123 nm; amplitude ~1e-7; eta pinned at 0 or 1) and must not be treated as physical. Crystalline phases are not yet identified; structure_matching/xrd on the low-T and high-T end members (passing refined FWHMs) is needed to assign the hydrate and anhydrous/product structures and confirm the transition assignment. The transition temperature (~44.6C) is bracketed only between 40.9 and 48.3C by the available sampling; finer temperature steps would sharpen it.
